title: Health & Wellness
description: Talk about health, fitness, nutrition, and preventive care. Discuss physical and mental well-being, visit the doctor, and understand medical advice. Master the present subjunctive for health-related wishes and the passive reflexive for health procedures.

vocabulary.source: my head hurts / I have a headache

grammar.title: Present Subjunctive for Health Wishes & Advice
grammar.content:
The present subjunctive is used to express wishes, hopes, advice, and recommendations — very common when talking about health:

Formation (regular):
-AR verbs: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en
-ER verbs: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an
-IR verbs: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an

Espero que te mejores pronto. (I hope you feel better soon.)
Quiero que descanses más. (I want you to rest more.)
Es importante que comas verduras. (It's important that you eat vegetables.)

Common irregular forms:
- ser → sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean
- estar → esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén
- ir → vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayáis, vayan
- saber → sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan
- tener → tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan
- poder → pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan
- hacer → haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagáis, hagan

Expressions that trigger the subjunctive:
- Espero que... (I hope that...)
- Quiero que... (I want that...)
- Es importante que... (It's important that...)
- Es necesario que... (It's necessary that...)
- Te recomiendo que... (I recommend that you...)
- Es bueno que... (It's good that...)
- Es malo que... (It's bad that...)
- Sugiero que... (I suggest that...)
- Deseo que... (I wish that...)
examples: Espero que tu padre se mejore de la operación. (I hope your father recovers from the surgery.)
Te recomiendo que hagas más ejercicio. (I recommend that you exercise more.)
Es importante que duermas ocho horas. (It's important that you sleep eight hours.)
Mi médico dice que no beba tanto café. (My doctor says I shouldn't drink so much coffee.)
Quiero que cuides tu salud mental. (I want you to take care of your mental health.)

grammar.title: Passive Reflexive (Se Pasiva) for Health Procedures
grammar.content:
The passive reflexive is used to describe health procedures, medical treatments, and general health facts without specifying who performs the action:

Structure: se + conjugated verb + noun (the 'subject')

The verb agrees with the noun that follows:

Se receta una pastilla. (A pill is prescribed.) — singular
Se recetan pastillas. (Pills are prescribed.) — plural
Se vacuna a los niños. (Children are vaccinated.)
Se operan los pacientes. (Patients are operated on.)

Health context examples:

Se recomienda hacer ejercicio diariamente. (Exercise is recommended daily.)
Se necesita una receta para el medicamento. (A prescription is needed for the medicine.)
Se practica yoga en el gimnasio. (Yoga is practiced at the gym.)
Se toman las vitaminas por la mañana. (Vitamins are taken in the morning.)

Note: When the noun is a person, use 'a' (personal a):
Se vacuna a los niños contra la gripe. (Children are vaccinated against the flu.)
Se opera a los pacientes cada mañana. (Patients are operated on every morning.)

This structure is very common in health information, medical websites, and wellness advice.
examples: Se recomienda beber ocho vasos de agua al día. (Eight glasses of water per day is recommended.)
Se practica natación en la piscina municipal. (Swimming is practiced at the municipal pool.)
Se vacuna a los niños a los dos años. (Children are vaccinated at age two.)
Se necesita reposo para recuperarse. (Rest is needed to recover.)
Se estudian las vitaminas en la escuela de medicina. (Vitamins are studied at medical school.)

grammar.title: Comparatives & Superlatives for Health Comparisons
grammar.content:
Comparatives and superlatives are used to compare health habits, conditions, and lifestyle choices:

Comparative structure:
- más + adjective/noun + que (more ... than)
- menos + adjective/noun + que (less ... than)
- tan + adjective/noun + como (as ... as)

Irregular comparatives:
- bueno → mejor (better)
- malo → peor (worse)
- grande → mayor (greater/larger)
- pequeño → menor (smaller/lesser)

Examples:
- Correr es más sano que estar sentado. (Running is healthier than sitting.)
- La fruta es más nutritiva que la comida chatarra. (Fruit is more nutritious than junk food.)
- El ejercicio es menos importante que el descanso. (Exercise is less important than rest.)
- Esta dieta es tan efectiva como la anterior. (This diet is as effective as the previous one.)

Superlative structure:
- el/la/los/las + más + adjective (+ de)
- el/la/los/las + menos + adjective (+ de)

Examples:
- El yoga es el mejor ejercicio para la mente. (Yoga is the best exercise for the mind.)
- La fruta es lo más nutritivo de la comida. (Fruit is the most nutritious thing to eat.)
- El descanso es lo menos importante para algunos. (Rest is the least important thing for some people.)

Irregular superlatives:
- bueno → el mejor (the best)
- malo → el peor (the worst)

Note: 'mejor' and 'peor' are invariable in gender but change in number (mejores, peores).
examples: La natación es el mejor ejercicio para las articulaciones. (Swimming is the best exercise for the joints.)
El azúcar es lo peor para la salud dental. (Sugar is the worst thing for dental health.)
El ejercicio es más importante que la dieta. (Exercise is more important than diet.)
La meditación es tan efectiva como el yoga para reducir el estrés. (Meditation is as effective as yoga for reducing stress.)
Comer frutas es lo más saludable que puedes hacer. (Eating fruit is the healthiest thing you can do.)

pronunciation.title: Stress Patterns in Health Vocabulary
pronunciation.content:
Key pronunciation rules for health and wellness vocabulary:

1. Palabras agudas (stress on last syllable) — marked if ending in consonant other than -n or -s:
   - el estrés (ES-trés) — has accent, ends in -s
   - la ansiedad (an-sie-DAD) — has accent, ends in -d
   - el insomnio (in-SOM-nyo) — no accent, ends in -o
   - la depresión (de-pre-SYON) — has accent, ends in -n

2. Palabras llanas (stress on penult) — marked if NOT ending in vowel, -n, or -s:
   - el gimnasio (gim-NAH-see-oh) — no accent, ends in -o
   - la nutrición (noo-tree-see-ON) — has accent, ends in -n
   - el ejercicio (e-her-SY-see-oh) — no accent, ends in -o
   - la alimentación (ah-lee-men-tah-SYON) — has accent, ends in -n

3. Palabras esdrújulas (stress on antepenult) — ALWAYS have an accent:
   - el análisis (ah-NA-lis) — wait, this is llana ending in -s, no accent: ah-NA-lis
   - Let me use correct examples:
   - la analítica (ah-nah-LEE-tee-kah) — llana, no accent
   - es-drú-ju-la (es-DROO-joo-lah) — esdrújula, always accented

4. Special health sounds:
   - -ción → -SYON: la nutrición (noo-tree-see-ON)
   - -sión → -SYON: la depresión (de-pre-SYON)
   - -mente (adverb ending) → MEN-te: mental (men-TAL)
   - -illo/-illa → Y-yo/yah: el ejercicio (e-her-SY-see-oh)

Key pronunciation practice words:
- salud = sah-LOOD (the 'u' is fully pronounced)
- bienestar = bye-en-ES-tar (stress on penult)
- estrés = ES-trés (stress on last, has accent)
- ejercicio = e-her-SY-see-oh (stress on penult)
- alimentación = ah-lee-men-tah-SYON (stress on -SYON)
- recuperación = roo-per-ah-SYON (stress on -SYON)
- ansiedad = an-sie-DAD (stress on last, has accent)
examples:
salud = sah-LOOD (stress on last syllable, no accent — ends in -d)
estrés = ES-trés (stress on last syllable, HAS accent — ends in -s)
ejercicio = e-jer-SY-see-oh (stress on penult, no accent — ends in -o)
depresión = de-pre-SYON (stress on last syllable, HAS accent — ends in -n)
ansiedad = an-sye-DAD (stress on last syllable, HAS accent — ends in -d)

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the correct present subjunctive? 'Es importante que tú ___ más verduras.' (It's important that you eat more vegetables.)
exercises.explanation: 'Comas' is the present subjunctive of 'comer' (tú form). After 'es importante que', we need the subjunctive mood because it expresses a recommendation. 'Comes' is indicative (present), 'comiste' is preterite, 'comerás' is future.

exercises.question: Complete with the subjunctive of 'estar': 'Espero que tú te ___ mejor pronto.' (I hope you feel better soon.)
exercises.explanation: 'Estés' is the present subjunctive tú form of 'estar'. 'Espero que' triggers the subjunctive because it expresses a hope/wish. 'Estar' is irregular in the subjunctive: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén.

exercises.question: What does 'Se recomienda hacer ejercicio' mean?
exercises.explanation: This is the passive reflexive (se pasiva): 'Exercise is recommended.' It doesn't specify WHO recommends it — it's a general health recommendation. The subject is 'hacer ejercicio' (to exercise) and the verb 'recomienda' agrees with it in singular.

exercises.question: Complete the comparative: 'El yoga es ___ sano que ver televisión.' (Yoga is healthier than watching TV.)
exercises.explanation: 'Más sano que' = 'healthier than'. The comparative structure is 'más + adjective + que'. The opposite would be 'menos sano que' (less healthy than).

exercises.question: What is the superlative of 'bueno'?
exercises.explanation: 'El mejor' is the irregular superlative of 'bueno' (the best). Spanish has several irregular comparatives and superlatives: bueno → mejor → el mejor; malo → peor → el peor.

exercises.question: Which word means 'anxiety' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La ansiedad' means anxiety. 'El estrés' is stress, 'la depresión' is depression, and 'el insomnio' is insomnia. All four are related to mental health but have distinct meanings.

exercises.question: Complete with the passive reflexive: '___ receta una pastilla para el dolor de cabeza.' (A pill is prescribed for headaches.)
exercises.explanation: 'Se receta' is the passive reflexive form. It means 'A pill is prescribed' without saying who prescribes it. The verb 'receta' agrees with 'una pastilla' (singular subject).

exercises.question: How do you say 'to have a fever' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Tener fiebre' = to have a fever. Don't confuse it with 'tener calor' (to be hot/hot weather) or 'tener frío' (to be cold). 'Fiebre' specifically refers to a medical fever.

exercises.question:
Match the Spanish health terms with their English meanings:

1. el resfriado
2. la gripe
3. la fiebre
4. el insomnio
exercises.explanation: el resfriado = cold; la gripe = flu; la fiebre = fever; el insomnio = insomnia. These are common health conditions you might discuss with a doctor.

exercises.question: Which is the correct passive reflexive for 'Children are vaccinated'? (Note the personal 'a')
exercises.explanation: 'Se vacuna a los niños' — the verb is singular ('vacuna') because the action is viewed as a general health practice (vaccination in general). The personal 'a' is required before 'los niños' because it refers to people. 'Se vacunan' would imply 'they are being vaccinated' as individual events.
